x: James H RIMMER · (Shropshire)

The first leg was run by Jim Rimmer who brought us in with 23rd position after falling heavily early on. Gerry North ran next and hurtled through the field to pull through to 7th, recording the fastest time.
James Rimmer and a new member,Michael Baker,were our other scorers in 100th and 133rd places respectively. Little change took place on the second lap.

Our other two scorers were Mike Baker, whose 195th place was a good effort in his first year of running, and Jim Rimmer who, when ahead of Baker, had two heavy falls that cost him 100 places in half a mile.
Jim Heathfield put in some useful running to take the handicap from Jim Rimmer ( a man to watch) who was a good second. Handicap Result: 1.J.Heathfield 26:13, 2.J.Rimmer 26:21, 3.D.Hurd 26:38
After his second placing in the '5¾' Jim Rimmer nearly caught the handicapper again with a praiseworthy 4th. You really will get your wings cut now Jim!
In the Belgrave Handicap,"old-stagers" Don Maclean and Mike Stearman tied for first place Third was that scourge of the handicapper, Jim Rimmer - he'll have his wings removed altogether soon!
Congratulations to the ever-present Laurie O'Hara who, in a good class field, was a praiseworthy 9th and to Jim Rimmer (48th) whose form is improving at an encouraging rate.
Jim Rimmer ( a man who could soon make our 'A' team if he works hard at it) picked up 4 places and the remaining four worked their way up to a praiseworthy 11th.

A dramatic finish was enacted between Ron Linstead and Jim Rimmer with "no one shall pass me" Linstead getting the verdict by the thickness of his number card and being incommunicado for the next five minutes.

The most notable performances amongst the remainder were by Bill Curtin and Jim Rimmer. The latter gave Bill a ten-seconds start, caught him after a half mile, towed him through the field for a further 1½ miles only to see the 15 years old Curtin run away from him in the closing stages.

Tony Brien a new junior member from Eire ran very well to finish eighth and took the handicap by a small margin from John Hall who is consistently improving with regular training. Jim Rimmer also ran well for third handicap place.
Other promising runs so far have come from Adrian Major, John Woodcock, Colin Pearson, John Hamilton, Mark McNair, Jim Rimmer and youths Bill Curtin and Richard Langley.

I'm worried about Jim - Rimmer that is - Three false starts in a non scoring 800 m at Battersea and he claimed Tony Brooks pushed him ... then the pistol failed to fire. - As Bill (MAN IN A SUITCASE) Kerr said, "the start was better than the race".

Worth noting was Jim Rimmer's good run in his first main outing of the season and Bob Glover's triumph over arch rival Brian Gorman. Although Gerry lost his title he nevertheless led Belgrave to victory again for the fourth successive year.

Trow, who ran some five minutes faster than anyone thought him capable and who was fast closing on Charlie Walker in the finishing straight. Jim Rimmer ran better than his fourth handicap place suggested so perhaps we will be seeing more of him than usual this season.
Other promising runs have come from Peter Carton, Bill Curtin, Bill Kerr, Adrian Major, Bob Smith and Jim Rimmer. This could be one of our stronger events.
TOP: CHARLIE GILLETT on his way to a Surrey Co. 400m H. title. BOTTOM LEFT: JIM RIMMER (14) is all set to win the Ryder Trophy 1500 metres BOTTOM RIGHT: GLYN RATCLIFFE, Belgrave shot putt champion.
Colin Pearson leads narrowly from John Thresher and Jim Rimmer with Guy Monnet, Laurie O'Hara, Mark McNair and John Keily following up in the Club 1500m championship.
Also very capable substitutes will be COLIN PEARSON and JIM RIMMER (saying "wait till the track season I'll show you") another useful youngster is RICHARD LANGLEY.
Back on the track, there signs of life returning to Track Captain Adrian Major, while in the 1,500m. Jim Rimmer and young Mark Clancy caught the eye.
Jimmy Rimmer is running with much more fire lately, and won the senior 1,500m. The senior track race providing the most excitement, however, was the 5,000m. team race.

Jim Rimmer had a good win in the 800m. in 1m. 58.9s., and Guy Monnet took the 3,000m. in 8m. 50.4s., while Philip Gee gave our quarter-miling strength a boost when he won the 400m. in a personal best time of 51.0s.
In the "B" 800m., Jim Rimmer confirmed that he, too, is now a power to be reckoned with, clocking the same time as the winner. Paddy Breslin made a good job of deputising for our star steeplechasers.

One of the highlights of the season has been the breakthrough of Jim Rimmer in the 1,500m. and 800m. Jim took second place in the Shropshire 1,500m. in a personal best 3m. 59.1s., a performance which won him County representative honours.
Philip Gee raced round one lap in 50.9s., Mel Ford covered two in 1m. 53.7s., and Colin Pearson broke the 2m. barrier with 1m. 59.7s., while Jim Rimmer lowered his 1,500m. best to 3m. 58.5s.
Jim Rimmer also had a first place in his group in the final straight, but had to give way to Melvern, of Windsor, in the final yards, though recording a personal best time.

Jim Rimmer confirmed his new "star" rating, by winning the 800m., and Bill Kerr won a surrealist steeplechase. Willie Williams was a hat-trick man in the junior events, while old rivals and team-mates John Stow and Bill Curtin shared the 800m. and 1,500m. titles, with John taking the former, and Bill the latter.
Steve White chalked up yet another sprint double, and Bill Kerr took the 1500m., while Jim Rimmer (3rd in 1m. 57.5s.) and John Boardman (fourth in 1m. 58s.) can be said to have run well in the 800m.
New star Jim Rimmer took the 1500m. in 4m. 04.5s., and to prove what a useful performance this was, we can say that Laurie O'Hara was third in 4m. 05.6s.
But Laurie O'Hara (18th in 8m. 20s.), and Jim Rimmer (24th in a personal best 8m. 30s.) produced a couple of first class performances to back John's.
Peter Carton ran a sound race in the 800m., as did Jim Rimmer in the 1500m. The usual crowd pulled together, doing two or three events apiece.

Jim Rimmer has been improving as fast this winter over the country as he did in the summer on the track. His performance in beating men like Trevor Hart, Alan Black and Pat O'Connor, as well as Bob Smith and Tony Fairclough, gave him a well deserved win in the handicap.
Jimmy Rimmer, in 93rd place, was the third Bel home - Pat O'Connor having finished 65th - and his performance promises even better in coming years.
As it was, Tony Brien won the Harry Parker Memorial Bowl, as our first man home, in 170th place, and Pat O'Connor and Jim Rimmer were our only other runners in the first 300.
Another fine run came from Jim Rimmer. Saying that he had just returned from holiday, he was placed in the 'B' team and produced our third fastest time.

Fortunately, Bob Smith and Jim Rimmer are going very well and Trevor Hart should repeat his 20th place of last year. Leading us home, we hope, will be Gerry North with his regular place inside the first ten.
The leaders of the pack in the 5¾ mile Club Championship road race at Wimbledon on 17th March. Yes, you're right, number 94 IS the legendary Jim Rimmer.
Front Page: James Rimmer, enjoying his most successful cross country season to date, on his way to a win in the Club 10 miles cross country championship.
Lionel Mann and Jim Rimmer were not far behind him over the first two laps but that last circuit was a real scorcher and our Captain came home with a clear one minute lead.

Gerry North also found it tough but nevertheless it suited him well and he once again qualified for the county team with a splendid run into 5th place. Jim Rimmer, another who has switched to Surrey, this time from Shropshire, ran particularly well to lead in the rest of our team.

A superb run by James Rimmer took him to his first Belgrave Championship over road or country and the handicap prize to boot. He looked impressive over the initial circuit as he took a handy lead from Lionel Mann, with Laurie O'Hara and Colin Pearson strung out behind.

There were some marvellous individual performances; our wins in the 100 and 200 metres, Jim Rimmer's return from the wilderness, Pete Carton under 2 minutes, Colin Pearson - a good double performance, another best from Leo Coy, youngsters Ronnie McCrossen and Michael Manning, two very good relay run…
Jim Rimmer, our holder of the Macher Shield, who, we hope, is going to have a horde after him eager to take the title. Arthur Welling, still active in performing and helping with the Veterans AC.
Jardine or Jim Rimmer. What's wrong with the intellectual talents of Paul Pringle and why can't Eddie Thorp or Alan Black display their talents of leadership?

John Stow, '5¾' Champion for 1975, started out for the Bels. and clocking our fastest time of the day over the long stage, handed over to Jim Rimmer in 14th position in the middle of a line of runners with less than half a minute covering them.

JUDY and JAMES RIMMER are another couple who are hearing the patter of tiny feet for the first time since DUNCAN JAMES was born in August. Let's hope he takes after Judy otherwise, if he patters those tiny feet too hard, he's sure to pick up his first achilles tendon injury before long!
Front page: James Rimmer hands over to Adrian Cook in the Surrey AC cross country relay.

When Jim Rimmer is trying to relax before a race tell him he looks bloody rough, ask him about his past injuries. ...... Tell Brian Gorman you are doing twice as much training as him, tell him his tan is disappearing and ask him if he has reached his 46th or 47th birthday yet.
Old twinkle-toes Laurie O'Hara picked his way best through the ankle wrenching ruts and came home at the head of the well spaced out pack with James Rimmer comfortably second.

James Rimmer romped away from the mediocre field completely unchallenged thanks to the now usual clash with the Mitcham 25Km road race. Only 40 seconds covered the three men in the hunt for the minor medals with Doug Maughan losing the silver to his (and everyone else's) arch-enemy Brian Gorman.
Bill Weller sends Jim Rimmer on his way for leg four of the Belgrave Harriers 'Haig' twelve stage relay.

Simon Holmes, the revelation of the winter season, added Jim Rimmer's scalp to his growing collection with a 'P.B.', and others to record their best times were Peter Hardwick and junior Pete Gardner who is maturing steadily into a most reliable runner.

Bill Weller and then Jim Rimmer pulled back five teams but newcomer Robin Brown was also not at his best and we were back to 23rd again. Robin is one of our most exciting prospects but perhaps a short lap would have been more suitable on this occasion.

Judy and Jim Rimmer had twins Owen and Stuart on April 18th - weighing in at seven and eight pounds apiece! Clare Louise made her entrance on June 28th, much to the pleasure of Jean and John Hamilton, and at around this time Jan and Martin Best produced a son, Luke.
: Jim Rimmer (keeping his shorts up on this occasion) lea[illegible] Leo Coy and Alan Black in the Surrey Cross Country Champs.
Colin Pearson, off 140 metres, chased by Simon Holmes, Jim Rimmer the back marker, and marathon man John Davies.

Ian Duncan was also absent, competing successfully in a University race, while Jim Rimmer seemed to have more than a little difficulty keeping his shorts on and even with second-claimer John Abberton of Poly H in our colours Ranelagh had no difficulty in beating us to the line.
Particular mention for a newcomer from New Zealand (actually born in Britain), Lyn Jones whose forceful running split Lionel Mann and Jim Rimmer.

Our team Captain was 52nd followed by Gerry North (making a very welcome appearance), Jim Rimmer and Leo Coy. With victory over Herne Hill by only 9 points we remained at the bottom of the league nearly 200 points adrift - requiring a really special effort from everyone to enable us to stay in the p…

Jim Rimmer was the only one to go with the two leaders but he was dropped after one lap and remained isolated in 3rd place. The second group of Gerry North, Lionel Mann, Colin Pearson and Simon Holmes were always falling back and the experience and fitness of Pat O'Connor and Tony Binda brought them…
After a fast downhill start Jim Rimmer led the Belgrave team followed by Alan Black, Leo Coy, Simon Holmes and Tom Dowdall - having a real 'blinder'.
Medallists in the 1979 Club '10' C.C. Championship. Left to right: Ian Duncan (1st), Laurie O'Hara (2nd) and Jim Rimmer (3rd).

If only Laurie O'Hara and Jim Rimmer could have made it... if only Dennis Brown, who was there, was qualified to run.... if only John Bicourt could have finished (he was 17th last year) .... if only Simon Williamson, running well but for Birmingham University as an individual, had been on our team .…

O'Hara, John Jackson, Lionel Mann, John Bicourt, Simon Holmes and Simon Williamson out of action for various reasons, it was left to the old team of Pat O'Connor and Jim Rimmer to lead the charge on our behalf.

Tony Binda, however, showed some improvement on his rather mediocre form of late by scoring an all too infrequent victory over Jim Rimmer and we also had a small consolation in that this year we did at least field a full team of nine runners!!

Clive Shippen to calculate results-go forward two places-Charlie Dabbs to assist-go back four places. Jim Rimmer enquiries-what time is the noon start? John Gladwin too young to run-agrees to hold crutches for Bill Laws who takes his place.
Submitting entries cost time and money and if people like Laurie O'Hara, Jim Rimmer, Pat O'Connor and Simon Holmes etc. can make it each time so could many others.

Worse was to follow in the race when after a very fine start Simon Williamson had an off day and rapidly dropped back down the field over the last half of the race, whilst an unfit John Gladwin and Jim Rimmer were unable to come to any solution.
29.00 · Jim Rimmer · Mar 73

This was in the Spring of 1968 when Colin was 25 and that summer he joined the likes of Jim Rimmer, John Martin, Adrian Major, John Kelly, Philip Gee, the Hamilton twins, Phil Smith and Alan Mead in some of the Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday sessions at Battersea track, organised by Tom Carter.
